name: Do You Need Duct Repair With AC Replacement?

mainEntity.name: How do I know if my air conditioning replacement needs ductwork repair too?
mainEntity.text: How do I know if my air conditioning replacement needs ductwork repair too?

acceptedAnswer.text: A new air conditioner will not solve comfort problems if the duct system is leaking, undersized, damaged, or badly routed. Signs that ductwork may need repair include rooms that never cool properly, weak airflow, strange noises, dust issues, and energy bills that stay high even after maintenance. In Los Angeles County, older homes and additions often have mixed duct conditions that reduce performance. A proper replacement estimate should include airflow testing, a look at duct condition, and a discussion of whether sealing, resizing, or replacing sections is needed. If ducts are not evaluated, the new unit may short-cycle, struggle to maintain temperature, or wear out faster.
acceptedAnswer.description: If the system has weak airflow, uneven cooling, high energy bills, noisy operation, or visible duct damage, the ducts may need repair along with the AC replacement. A new unit cannot perform well if the ducts leak, collapse, or are poorly sized. Duct inspection should be part of the replacement estimate when comfort problems already exist.
